assumptions.text: Lending is the only core: both goals (G1 on-time returns, G2 fees collected) move on lending's rules and reminders; fees is scored 6/5 and stays supporting under rule 3.
Membership is 'product' evolution but sourced build: a membership SaaS would not feed the eligibility rule or keep GDPR data (C4) inside the one Postgres (C3); it is three tables and a form.
Card payments (commodity) are an adapter inside fees and membership - transaction-script glue around Stripe, never a model of Stripe's problem (understand N3, C1).
No history-as-asset need: disputes over a fee are settled by the coordinator waiving it, so an append-only ledger table is enough and event sourcing is not justified.

open_questions.text: Would the library accept myTurn (or similar) for membership and catalogue if lending and fees were built around it, or must everything be one system?
Do fee disputes happen often enough that a full history of every balance change (event-sourced ledger) would pay for itself?

classifications.rationale: core - G1 (90% returned on time) is won or lost on reservation holds, the 14-day loan, one renewal and the three-item / no-overdue eligibility rule; today's alternative: the spreadsheet and paper book (alt-spreadsheet-signout) and myTurn's generic loan rules; rule 2 (diff >= 7); cplx 6 from time-driven state (hold expiry, due, overdue), eligibility assembled from three contexts and the renewal-only-if-unreserved rule.
classifications.future_direction: decisive core; stays core - review in 12 months whether reminders alone deliver G1 and whether the rules need a smarter allocation (waiting lists).

classifications.rationale: supporting - G2 (80% of fees paid in 30 days) depends on it, but the rules (GBP 1 a day, cap at replacement value, waiver) are small; today's alternative: the cash tin and nobody chasing (alt-spreadsheet-signout); rule 3 (diff 6, cplx 5 < 6); cplx 5 from daily accrual, the cap and two payment channels; card capture is a commodity adapter (Stripe, C1).
classifications.future_direction: stays supporting; a ledger table with append-only rows; move to an event-sourced ledger only if disputes become common (Q2).

classifications.rationale: supporting - no goal metric names it (goal_ids []), but lending cannot lend what inventory does not declare fit; today's alternative: the spreadsheet's tool tab (alt-spreadsheet-signout) and myTurn's catalogue; rule 3; cplx 4 from the item lifecycle (tagged, fit, in maintenance, retired) and the kind/unit split.
classifications.future_direction: stays supporting; keep to a lifecycle with a status column; if catalogue browsing grows a public face, split the catalogue out (decompose Q2).

classifications.rationale: supporting - no goal metric names it (goal_ids []); it must work, nobody notices excellence; today's alternative: myTurn (alt-myturn) does this well; rule 3 (diff 3, and not solved by an integrated system, so not generic); built rather than bought because C3 (one Postgres, one web application) and C4 (GDPR data in one place) make a separate membership product cost more than the three tables it replaces; cplx 3 from concession approval and lapsing.
classifications.future_direction: table-stakes; keep as forms over data; revisit buying if the library federates with others (a non-goal today).

bets.text: Reminders two days before and on the due date, plus a blocked check-out when overdue, are enough to lift on-time returns from today's guess of ~60% to 90%.
bets.risk: If members ignore email, G1 needs a different lever (SMS, deposits) and the lending rules change.
bets.validate_by: on-time share after 3 months of live loans

plain_words.what: We decided where the design effort goes and what to buy instead of build.
plain_words.decided: Lending is the one core and gets a real model with tested rules. Fees, inventory and membership are kept simple. Card payments are Stripe behind a thin adapter.
plain_words.assumed: That fees is not a core: its rules are small and the goal it serves (fees collected) is mostly about lending blocking borrowers who owe money.
plain_words.riskiest: If fees turns out to be where the arguments are (disputes, waivers, cash versus card), it was under-invested and will need a rewrite into a proper ledger.
